candidate.name: intraday_close_transition_range_quadratic_efficiency_238p
candidate.mechanism: Allocation of completed-session quadratic price variation between within-half adjacent closing-level transitions and the contemporaneous destination bars' intrabar high-low excursions.
candidate.formula: For 119 pairs in each half set c_j=ln(close_j/close_j-1), h_j=ln(high_j/low_j), Q=sum(c_j^2), H=sum(h_j^2), and score Q/(Q+H).
candidate.fixed_support: Exactly 238 within-half pairs from the fixed 240 standard bars; exclude 09:30 and the lunch transition; never bridge dates, stocks, or halves.
candidate.zero_and_missing_semantics: Retain exact-zero transitions and ranges. Require all selected high/low/close values finite and positive with low<=close<=high and finite Q+H>0. Never drop a pair, add epsilon, fill, clip, threshold, or substitute.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_interbar_gap_discovery_share_238p
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: Both allocate boundary-scale movement against destination high-low range on 238 within-half opportunities.
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Campaign092 reads open and prior close, uses absolute first-power open gaps and linear ranges. Campaign093 never reads open, uses adjacent closes, and compares squared transition and squared range variation. Holding every open gap fixed while changing a destination close changes Campaign093 but not Campaign092 when destination ranges are preserved.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_intrabar_body_range_efficiency_240m
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: Both compare price movement with high-low range.
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: The terminal factor uses same-bar absolute open-close bodies and linear ratio-of-sums across 240 bars. Campaign093 uses adjacent close transitions, no open, quadratic terms, and 238 matched destination opportunities.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_diffusive_variation_ratio_238m and intraday_bipower_jump_variation_share_238m
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Those terminal factors compare realized close variance with adjacent-return bipower variation to characterize diffusion or jumps. Campaign093 uses no bipower product and compares close-transition quadratic variation with observed intrabar high-low quadratic excursions.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_five_minute_variance_ratio_230w
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: The terminal factor compares overlapping five-return sums with one-minute return variance using close only. Campaign093 keeps the one-minute grid and introduces high-low excursion variation; it performs no aggregation to another sampling horizon.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_realized_volatility
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: The numerator contains one-minute close-transition realized variation.
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Raw realized volatility changes under a common scaling of all return magnitudes, whereas Campaign093 is an allocation share invariant when close-transition and range magnitudes scale together. The high-low denominator is essential and no volatility level is selected.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: intraday_intrabar_range_participation_entropy_240m, intraday_range_clock_center_240m, and intraday_range_amount_profile_alignment_js_240m
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Those factors measure range distribution, timing, or amount alignment. Campaign093 discards clock and amount allocation after pooling squared ranges and changes when close-transition quadratic variation changes while the range profile stays fixed.

nearest_semantic_challenges.name: candidate49_intraday_cumulative_vwap_crossing_rate_240m_v1
nearest_semantic_challenges.relationship: Both use the completed standard-minute grid.
nearest_semantic_challenges.distinction: Candidate49 counts causal close-versus-cumulative-VWAP sign crossings and requires volume/amount. Campaign093 uses high/low/close variation only, never constructs VWAP, and never touches the prospective ledgers.
